submission.natural_language_explanation: Retrospective lexical detector: N808+ fires on the current token when that token is a word of appraisal, prominence or degree — praise or criticism (great, amazing, favorite, fantastic, horrible, excellent), claims of notice (famous, renowned, notable, prominent) and magnitude/emphasis/certainty words (huge, gigantic, biggest, greatest, more, very, possible, typical, normal, own, same) — and sits at or below zero on neutral naming words (salt, butter, table, window, river, algorithm, serum, rain, glass, bland, unknown, tiny). The same positions fire roughly 0.3–0.4 higher inside a food/cooking passage, which is what lifts recipe-step tokens such as ' Pour' (0.4 outside a recipe vs 1.5 inside one) to the neuron's peaks.

rival_explanations: Positive-sentiment detector: the pole fires only on praise and approval (great, amazing, favorite, excellent), so on new text it is silent on ' horrible', ' awful', ' unacceptable', ' huge' and ' possible' and stays high on ' wonderful' and ' love' whatever their degree or prominence.

Food/cooking register neuron: the real driver is the recipe/description context, not the token class, so the pole fires on ingredient and cooking-instruction tokens in any non-food-free passage and is silent on evaluative prose that is not about food or enthusiastic narration.

Rare-or-marked-word detector: the pole fires on any statistically marked, low-frequency content word regardless of evaluation, so it should be just as active on rare technical nouns (serum, algorithm, membrane) and narrative words (rain, glass, grey) as on ' famous' or ' notable'.

The journey of a child’s language development begins as early as birth; and the first 12 months are an important stage of this development. Parents, grandparents, siblings, caregivers, aunt, uncles…everyone involved in your baby’s world is introducing communication each day and can be a part of the journey. There are so many ways to help with your child’s speech development. While sometimes it may feel one-sided, like you’re talking to yourself, you’re not. For some of us, thinking out loud doesn’t come as naturally. Here are a few simple tricks and activities to keep a steady stream of language flowing in your everyday baby interactions:
- Talk to baby frequently, about everything.
Try narrating your day together: Now let’s count the snaps on your jammies, “1, 2, 3, 4…4 snaps!” Or point to the items and tools of the day, “How about some banana?” (Pointing at the fruit)
- Respond to them talking to you.
Crying, eye contact, coos, gurgles, grunts, babble, smiles, and waving arms and feet are all your baby’s way of talking and communicating for more cuddles, no more cuddles, hungry, not hungry, tired, not tired enough, and sometimes just to grab your attention. Your response let’s your baby know you’re listening and encourages her to communicate more in return.
- Introduce new words.
Don’t be afraid to use new words and use them frequently. Repetition will allow baby to take in and work to understand what you are saying.
- Read books!
Research shows reading to a child every helps them in language development along with other developmental areas. Baby’s first board books, your childhood favorites, touch and feel, wordless (you make up the words) – read whatever makes it fun for you and for baby. Follow baby’s lead and increase or decrease depending on her interest (cries, coos, kicks…(see “Crying” above)
Songs, melodies, choruses and rhymes are fun ways to help your baby listen for and recognized words.
Peek-a-boo or playing hide-and-seek with objects is a way to teach names of objects. Children learn through play at every stage of their development.
Always keep in mind that all babies develop at different rates. Just because baby might not be doing what your friend’s baby is doing at six month isn’t necessarily cause for alarm. Talk to your doctor or YWCA Consultant to learn about your babies development and to answer your questions or concerns. “Raising Children” is a another resource for age groups and corresponding developmental milestones.

Prader-willi syndrome is a genetic disorder caused by loss of a portion of a copy of chromosome 15. Common features include early problems with muscle weakness and feeding followed by occult weight gain without an increase in food consumption beginning during late infancy/early toddler period prior to the onset of hyperphagia. Recent research has shown a role for changes in the balance of gut bacteria in weight gain (human and animal), and hyperphagia (animal) studies. The altered gut bacteria balance allows more absorption of calories with increased weight gain on fixed oral calories. We hypothesize that individuals with Prader-willi syndrome have an altered balance in gut bacteria which may influence weight gain and appetite. We propose a pilot study of the gut microbiome among individuals with Prader-willi syndrome focusing on twins (identical twins and fraternal twins) in addition to prospective collection of stool specimens focused upon infants/young children with Prader-willi syndrome moving through age associated dietary changes to assess whether alterations in the gut microbiome may contribute to weight discrepancies and reported differences in hyperphagic tendencies reported by families. If there is alteration in gut bacteria found in PWS, interventions which can change the balance of gut bacteria may be beneficial.
Robert Shulman, MD
Baylor College of Medicine

Peptidergic excitation of supraoptic nucleus neurons: involvement of stretch-inactivated cation channels.
Although the primary stimulus regulating vasopressin (VP) release is a change in systemic osmolality, other physiological parameters are known to affect VP secretion or modulate the osmotic control over its release. Neuropeptides feature prominently in afferents underlying the central regulation of the VP-releasing magnocellular neurosecretory cells (MNCs). Although little is yet known of the circumstances under which peptides are released onto MNCs, previous studies have shown that a common response profile to exogenous peptide application is a slow excitation that seems to result from the activation of a nonselective cation conductance. In this paper we review the basis for the excitatory effects of angiotensin II, cholecystokinin, and neurotensin in MNCs acutely isolated from the supraoptic nucleus of adult rats. Saturating concentrations of these three peptides evoked nonadditive increases in macroscopic cation conductance. During single-channel recordings Ang II, CCK, and NT caused kinetically identical increases in the probability of opening of 35-pS nonselective cation channels. Patches containing only one channel further revealed that the activity of single channels could be regulated by separate applications of all three peptides. Peptide-stimulated channels were also found to be inactivated by increases in membrane stretch and to be blocked by low concentrations of gadolinium (Gd(3+)). It is concluded that many excitatory peptides depolarize MNCs by stimulating the stretch-inactivated cation channels underlying osmoreception. Convergent regulation of these channels provides a potentially powerful mechanism for integrating signals derived from the various afferents involved in the regulation of MNCs.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The table stood by the window, and through the glass the river and the rain looked grey all afternoon while the kettle cooled on the sill and nobody spoke.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis names table, window, glass, river and rain as neutral naming words sitting at or below zero, so this scene should not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The algorithm flagged the serum sample after the readings drifted outside the range printed on the label beside the machine, so the operator repeated the run.
adversarial_test_results.detail: algorithm and serum are on the hypothesis's own neutral naming list and the sentence makes no appraisal, prominence or degree claim.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The stew was bland and the portion was tiny for the price we paid at the counter near the station, and we left without finishing it.
adversarial_test_results.detail: bland and tiny are both on the hypothesis's neutral naming list predicted at or below zero even though one is criticism and one is degree, so this tests its stated word list directly.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The cause of the outage remains unknown and the engineers are still reviewing the logs from the servers overnight before they publish a report.
adversarial_test_results.detail: unknown is a named neutral word and the rest is a plain factual report with no appraisal, prominence or degree token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Combine the flour and water in a bowl, stir for a minute, then cover the bowl and leave it for twenty minutes before shaping the dough.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A recipe passage carrying only neutral naming and instruction words: the claimed 0.3-0.4 food lift cannot raise flour, water or bowl to the peak, so the hypothesis predicts silence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Bake the potatoes at 200 degrees for forty minutes, turning them once halfway through the cooking time on the middle shelf of the oven.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Another cooking instruction with numbers and neutral nouns but no appraisal, degree or 'Pour' token, so the food lift alone should not fire it.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The site instructions for the foundation are posted in the office. Pour the concrete into the mould and leave it to harden overnight before the next stage begins.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The exact claimed peak token ' Pour' outside any recipe and with no appraisal or degree word nearby; the hypothesis puts such positions near 0.4 rather than at the peak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She poured the last of her savings into the small shop and told nobody for a year while the debt grew and the customers stayed away.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The same word in its past-tense metaphorical sense with no appraisal, degree or cooking frame, which the hypothesis says should stay low.

Case No. 19-4471

Opinion filed March 2, 2021

Before the court the motion was filed on time and the clerk stamped it in the record.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Delimiter control (Sun et al.): the claimed peak token '\n\n' sits in a court heading with no retrospective appraisal anywhere, so the token-class account predicts no fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The bus left at nine and the driver said the road ahead was closed, so we waited in the station until noon and read the notices.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Everyday narrative of common words with no appraisal, prominence or degree token, a check that the unit is not simply always active on prose.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The spectrometer measured absorbance of the supernatant at 340 nanometres before the centrifuge stopped and the technician logged the result in the register.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Rare technical nouns (spectrometer, supernatant, centrifuge) with no evaluation, which the hypothesis predicts is silent.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: A grey heron stood motionless in the reeds at the edge of the mere while the mist rose over the water and the light failed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Marked narrative vocabulary (heron, reeds, mere, mist) with no appraisal or degree word, predicted silent by the hypothesis.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The favorite drifted in the betting market and finished fourth in the five-furlong sprint on soft ground in front of a small crowd.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same word, other sense: the claimed token ' favorite' here is the horse with the shortest odds, not a word of appraisal, so the hypothesis's reading should not fire on it.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The board named her a possible for the regional post but would not discuss the shortlist before the meeting in June.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same word, other sense: ' possible' as a noun meaning a candidate is not a certainty modifier, so the hypothesis predicts no fire even though the claimed token is present.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They own the building on the corner and rent the lower floor to a bakery that opens early and closes before dark.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'own' as a main verb rather than the emphatic possessive the hypothesis lists under emphasis, so its degree reading should not fire on the verb.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The gap between the metal plates is tiny, about two microns wide at room temperature, and the seal must sit flush.
adversarial_test_results.detail: tiny is on the hypothesis's neutral naming list, so this measurement sentence tests whether it really sits at or below zero despite being a degree word.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They agreed to table the motion until the next session of the council met in the autumn and the budget had been agreed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'table' in its verb sense (to postpone), a neutral naming word the hypothesis predicts is silent.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The team scored twice in the second half and the match ended at four to two in front of a small crowd on a wet pitch.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A plain sports result with no appraisal, prominence or degree token, predicted silent.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: La mesa está junto a la ventana y el río se ve a través del cristal empañado de la cocina al fondo del pasillo.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Spanish hard negative mirroring the English naming-word probes: mesa, ventana, río and cristal are naming words and every fragment here is non-evaluative, so the hypothesis predicts no fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It was noted at the hearing that the file had been sent late and the clerk agreed to check the record before the next sitting.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'noted' as a procedural reporting verb, not a claim of notice or prominence, so the prominence class should not fire here.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The service at the hotel was horrible and the room smelled of damp, so we asked to move to another floor near the back.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Criticism is claimed to fire alongside praise, so the hypothesis predicts active on 'horrible' in a non-food passage.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: His behaviour at the meeting was unacceptable and the chair asked him to leave the room before the vote on the budget.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Second criticism holdout with the new appraisal word 'unacceptable', predicted active by the praise-or-criticism reading.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The bridge rests on a huge concrete pier that carries the weight of the entire span across the valley in winter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: huge is a claimed magnitude word in a neutral engineering description, so the hypothesis predicts active without any food context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It is very cold today and the streets are quiet because of the holiday and the early closing of the shops.
adversarial_test_results.detail: very is a claimed degree word in a plain weather report, predicted active by the degree class.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Each child took their own bag and followed the same route to the school gate as the year before, past the mill and the bridge.
adversarial_test_results.detail: own and same are listed emphasis words, so the hypothesis predicts active on this possessive and identity sentence that contains no praise at all.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She is a renowned architect whose work is taught in universities across the country and written about in several books.
adversarial_test_results.detail: renowned belongs to the claimed class of claims of notice, tested in a new non-food context, so the hypothesis predicts active.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The view from the ridge was splendid, an immense sweep of moorland under a pale sky, and the walk up took an hour from the road.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Paraphrase holdout: splendid and immense express praise and magnitude with words absent from the top examples, predicted active.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: This year's harvest was bigger than last year's, and the granary is nearly full for the first time in a decade of poor summers.
adversarial_test_results.detail: bigger is a comparative magnitude word of the same class as the listed biggest and more, predicted active in a farming context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It is possible that the evening train will be delayed by the engineering works, so allow half an hour for the connection at the junction in the timetable.
adversarial_test_results.detail: possible in its modal sense is a listed certainty word in a plain travel notice, so the hypothesis predicts active, while the positive-sentiment rival names ' possible' as one it should miss.
